home_page.carousel_welcome_text: An innovative e-learning platform that uses artificial intelligence to support mathematical learning, adapting to each student's needs, learning pace, and goals.
home_page.carousel_olympiads_text: A dedicated learning space designed to support students preparing effectively for challenges and Olympiads.
home_page.carousel_system_text: Uses an exclusive recommendation algorithm to dynamically adapt the learning experience and meet each individual's unique needs and preferences.
home_page.mathe_description: Is an adaptive and open-access platform designed to empower students and educators through personalized mathematical learning, offering adaptive assessments, interactive resources, and AI-supported tools that enrich the learning experience, strengthen mathematical understanding, and promote academic success.
home_page.objective1: Offer free access to an AI-driven learning platform designed to enhance mathematical understanding and engagement.
home_page.objective2: Provide diverse learning resources, including written materials and video lessons.
home_page.objective3: Support both independent learning and collaborative educational experiences.
home_page.objective4: Identify areas where students excel and areas requiring additional support.
home_page.mathe_higher_education_desc: The MathE Higher Education provides a personalized learning environment designed to support students in overcoming mathematical challenges and progressing at their own pace.
home_page.mathe_olympiads_desc: The MathE Olympiads provides students with access to scientific challenges from different countries, encouraging excellence, critical thinking, and international engagement in mathematics.
home_page.stay_up_to_date: Stay up to date with the latest from MathE
home_page.mathe_present_in_countries: MathE is already present in {{count}} countries.

higher_education.description: The MathE Higher Education is a space dedicated to students and teachers in higher education. The platform features a recommendation system developed and trained to help students overcome difficulties in Mathematics and support their learning and progress at their own pace, in a personalized and efficient way.
higher_education.objective1: Help students to overcome difficulties and strengthen their mathematical skills effectively.
higher_education.objective2: Allow advanced students to progress through complex content at their own pace in a personalized way.
higher_education.objective3: Encourage autonomy in the learning process, stimulating students to develop independent and continuous study habits.
higher_education.objective4: Identify the specific difficulties of each student through personalized recommendations.
higher_education.objective5: Offer content and exercises appropriate to the individual's learning profile.
higher_education.available_contents_desc: The collection of mathematical resources are organized by topic, subtopic, and keywords to help you find what you need.
higher_education.detailed_desc_unavailable: Detailed description regarding this specific content is currently unavailable.
higher_education.assessment_desc: Assessment enables students to evaluate their knowledge on a selected Math topic.
higher_education.library_desc: Library provides a set of written and videos materials to support the learning process.
higher_education.performance_desc: Provides an overview of your performance across all activities you have completed.

home_page_olympiad.mathe_olympiads_desc: The MathE Olympiads is a space designed for students interested in academic challenges. The platform provides access to extensive question banks from scientific contests and olympiads from several countries, enabling students to prepare effectively through personalized learning resources and practice tools.
home_page_olympiad.objective1: Promote and encourage the study of mathematics through academic challenges and Olympiads.
home_page_olympiad.objective2: Democratize access to mathematics challenges, particularly for students in underserved areas.
home_page_olympiad.objective3: Support students in preparing for scientific challenges through high-quality learning materials, practice exercises, and personalized resources.
home_page_olympiad.objective4: Foster problem-solving and mathematical reasoning skills through engaging and challenging learning experiences.
home_page_olympiad.mathe_info_olympiads_desc: The MathE Olympiads is an enrichment initiative designed to challenge and inspire students with an interest in mathematics.
home_page_olympiad.performance_desc2: Track your progress with a comprehensive overview of all completed activities, helping you identify strengths, monitor improvement, and focus on areas needing further development.

learning_style_page.title: Learning Style
learning_style_page.choose_hint: Answer a few quick questions and see how you prefer to learn.

kolb.description: A questionnaire based on Kolb's learning cycle.

active.name: Active
active.summary: You learn best by trying things out.

reflective.name: Reflective
reflective.summary: You learn best by thinking it through first.

sensing.name: Sensing
sensing.summary: You prefer concrete examples and clear procedures.

intuitive.name: Intuitive
intuitive.summary: You prefer concepts, patterns and the idea behind them.

visual.name: Visual
visual.summary: You prefer diagrams, graphs and videos.

verbal.name: Verbal
verbal.summary: You prefer written and spoken explanations.

sequential.name: Sequential
sequential.summary: You prefer to go step by step.

global.name: Global
global.summary: You prefer to see the big picture first.

q1.text: When I do not understand a math question, I prefer to:
q1.a: Try a similar exercise with some guidance.
q1.b: Read an explanation before trying again.

q2.text: I understand formulas better when I see:
q2.a: A numerical example using concrete values.
q2.b: The general idea behind the formula.

q3.text: Before solving a difficult question, I prefer to see:
q3.a: A diagram, graph, image or video.

q4.text: When starting a new topic, I prefer to:
q4.a: Follow the content step by step.
q4.b: First understand the general idea of the topic.

q5.text: After making a mistake, I prefer the platform to:
q5.a: Give me another easier question immediately.
q5.b: Show me why my answer was wrong first.

q6.a: Follow a clear method or known procedure.
q6.b: Make me discover patterns or relationships.

q7.text: A solution is clearer to me when it has:
q7.a: Visual separation of steps, arrows or highlighted parts.
q7.b: Detailed written sentences explaining each step.

q8.text: When I get confused, I prefer:
q8.a: Going back to the previous step.

q9.text: I learn mathematics better when I:
q9.a: Start practicing with exercises as soon as possible.
q9.b: Think about the concept before solving exercises.

q10.text: When learning a new concept, I prefer:
q10.b: A conceptual explanation of how the idea works.

q11.text: I remember mathematical ideas better when they are presented as:

q12.text: Before an assessment, I would prefer to:
q12.a: Review the basic steps needed to solve the exercises.
q12.b: See an overview of what the assessment is about.

q13.text: When studying a new topic, I usually prefer to:
q13.a: Work through examples and learn while doing.
q13.b: Pause and review the explanation carefully.

q14.text: A mathematical explanation is clearer when it:
q14.a: Uses the exact values from the problem.

q15.text: When reviewing a topic, I would rather use:
q15.a: A video lesson or visual summary.
q15.b: A teaching material with written explanation.

q16.text: I learn better when the platform:
q16.a: Shows one small concept at a time.
q16.b: Shows how the topic connects with other topics.

q17.text: During a study session, I feel more comfortable when I can:
q17.a: Interact with questions and receive quick feedback.
q17.b: Analyze the material quietly before answering.

q18.text: When solving exercises, I prefer to:
q18.a: Apply a procedure step by step.
q18.b: Look for the underlying pattern or shortcut.

q19.text: When a formula is introduced, I prefer:
q19.a: A visual representation of what it means.
q19.b: A written explanation of each term.

q20.text: When studying a topic such as Analytic Geometry, I prefer to:
q20.a: Start with bases and vector operations before harder subtopics.
q20.b: See how vectors, lines, planes and distances are connected first.

q21.text: If I get a wrong answer, I usually want to:
q21.a: Try again with a new question.
q21.b: Understand the reason for the error first.

q22.text: I feel more confident when a solution shows:
q22.b: The general reasoning behind the method.

q23.text: I usually understand a topic faster when the platform shows:

q24.text: A study path is more useful to me when it:
q24.a: Gives me a fixed order to follow.
q24.b: Lets me choose from a topic map after seeing the whole structure.

q25.text: I remember a method better when I:
q25.b: Review the logic behind it first.

q26.text: I usually prefer examples that are:
q26.a: Specific and close to the exercise.
q26.b: General and connected to wider ideas.

q27.text: If I need help with a question, I prefer:
q27.a: A visual hint or highlighted solution path.
q27.b: A written hint explaining what to do.

q28.text: When I solve exercises, I prefer:
q28.a: Questions that gradually increase in complexity.
q28.b: Questions that help me understand the overall topic.

q29.text: When I am unsure about a topic, I prefer:
q29.a: A short hint followed by another attempt.
q29.b: A more complete explanation before continuing.

q30.text: When I review an answer, I want to know:
q30.a: Which steps and numbers lead to the result.
q30.b: Why the chosen method works in general.

q31.text: I find it easier to compare concepts using:

q32.text: When using a learning platform, I prefer:
q32.a: A guided route through the content.
q32.b: A general map where I can see all related subtopics.

q33.text: In an online learning platform, I prefer to:
q33.a: Learn by answering questions and checking feedback.
q33.b: Learn by reviewing explanations and then answering.

q34.text: I prefer learning materials that include:

q35.text: When I study from online materials, I prefer:

q36.text: When a concept is difficult, I prefer the platform to:
q36.b: Show how it fits into the topic as a whole.

q37.text: When I see a solved example, I prefer to:
q37.a: Try a similar example right away.
q37.b: Read the full reasoning before trying another one.

q38.a: Clear rules that I can apply directly.
q38.b: Abstract ideas that explain several cases.

q39.text: A difficult topic becomes clearer when I can:
q39.b: Read a detailed explanation about it.

q40.text: I feel more confident when learning starts with:

q41.text: I feel I learn more when the platform:
q41.b: Gives me time to review and think.

q42.text: When the platform gives feedback, I prefer it to:
q42.a: Use a concrete example from the question.
q42.b: Explain the main concept behind the question.

q43.text: When the platform recommends support material, I prefer:

q44.text: To review after a mistake, I prefer:
